title: Button Design
subtopics: Hover, focus, active, and disabled states
learning_outcomes: Describe the role of Button Design and recognize when it is useful.
Apply a relevant property, selector, or technique from this lesson in a small stylesheet.
Inspect the browser result and explain one behavior, limitation, or compatibility consideration.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore Button Design through a small CSS example, a visual guide, and one practical check. You do not need to memorize every property at once; focus on the decision the browser is making.
content.why_it_matters: Button Design helps you build interfaces that remain understandable, maintainable, and usable as content and viewport conditions change.

content_blocks.title: Interactive control states
content_blocks.alt_text: Design each meaningful state and preserve visible keyboard focus. Labels show the concept flow.
content_blocks.caption: Use the labeled steps as a reasoning guide; detailed behavior is described in the lesson.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: An interface needs more than a default appearance: design default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, and invalid states where relevant. Never remove keyboard focus indicators without a clear replacement.

content_blocks.title: A useful way to practice
content_blocks.text: Start with one element or component. Use the concepts in this lesson—primary, secondary, and tertiary styles, hover, focus, active, and disabled states, loading indicators—and change one declaration at a time. Compare the page before and after the change.

items.title: Primary, secondary, and tertiary styles
items.text: Connect primary, secondary, and tertiary styles to the main idea in button design, then verify it in a minimal browser example.

items.title: Hover, focus, active, and disabled states
items.text: Check the experience with keyboard-only interaction, text zoom, high contrast settings, and more than one viewport.

items.title: Loading indicators
items.text: Connect loading indicators to the main idea in button design, then verify it in a minimal browser example.

items.title: Icon buttons
items.text: Connect icon buttons to the main idea in button design, then verify it in a minimal browser example.

items.title: Consistent button dimensions
items.text: Calculate the rendered box, not only its declared width; check padding, border, min/max constraints, and the parent layout.

content_blocks.expected_output: The sample has distinct hover, keyboard-focus, and disabled states; focus remains visible without relying on color alone.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Put this snippet in styles.css and link it from a minimal index.html file with a viewport meta tag. Add elements whose classes match the selectors, open the page in a modern browser, and inspect computed styles. This lesson editor displays the expected result as a guide; it is not a server-side arbitrary-code runner.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original CSS snippet, save the file, and repeat the test. Remove temporary debugging rules before keeping a final version.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Use the smallest valid example, prefer a readable default, and check browser behavior rather than trusting appearance alone.

content.task: Try it yourself: build a small example that demonstrates Button Design. Use the simplest relevant selector and one or more declarations, inspect the browser result, and explain it in your own words.
task_acceptance_criteria: The stylesheet uses valid CSS syntax for the chosen feature.
The intended element or state visibly changes when the rule applies.
The behavior is checked with browser tools or a documented manual checklist.
hints: Write the smallest rule that can demonstrate the concept.
Inspect which element matched and which declaration won before adding more selectors.
For a developing or optional feature, check browser support and preserve a useful fallback.
content.expected_output: The sample has distinct hover, keyboard-focus, and disabled states; focus remains visible without relying on color alone.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to connect a visual change to its cause.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one property, save, and compare again.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the last rule always wins.
common_mistakes.why: The cascade also considers origin, importance, layers and selector specificity; scope and source order may also matter.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect matched declarations and computed styles before changing the stylesheet.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only one viewport or interaction state.
common_mistakes.why: A rule can work at one width and fail when content, focus, zoom or preferences change.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the check at narrow and wide widths and include keyboard focus or reduced-motion checks when relevant.

summary: Button Design is easiest to learn by connecting syntax to a rendered result.
Keep selectors readable and test the effect in the browser.
Verify compatibility and accessibility when the feature or interface requires it.
